I am a Lecturer (Assistant Professor) in the [Department of Economics, University of Exeter](http://business-school.exeter.ac.uk/about/departments/economics/). My other affiliations include: research associate at Harvard University's [Culture, Cognition, Coevolution Lab](https://coevolution.fas.harvard.edu/current-lab-members), and affiliate fellow at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business's [Stigler Center](https://www.chicagobooth.edu/research/stigler/research/affiliate-fellows/current-cohort). I hold a PhD in economics from the University of Zurich.

I study how culture and institutions shape economic and political development — and how they are, in turn, reshaped by markets, migration, and crises. My work combines large-scale historical data (newspapers, censuses, patents) with field experiments, spanning political economy, economic development, economic history, and cultural evolution.

My research has been published in the *Journal of Political Economy* and is forthcoming in the *Journal of the European Economic Association*. Some of my earlier work appeared under my former name, Max Winkler.
